news.title: Ultracold atoms could help unravel a major flaw in quantum theory
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print Extremely cold atoms form a state of matter called a Bose-Einstein condensate NIST Extremely cold atoms could help physicists answer a long-debated question about quantum particles and time. This may shed light on the accuracy of different interpretations of quantum physics.

When it comes to time, quantum physics fails to answer even the simplest questions. For instance, predicting how long it will take a quantum particle to travel from some point A to a nearby point B has been debated since quantum theory’s earliest days.

news.title: AI solved the hardest problem in maths – is there anything it can’t do?
paras: In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths .

The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name.

news.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
paras: Bog down Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming Detailed estimate going back to 1800 shows how much carbon is being liberated. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions.

Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

news.title: From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices
paras: Our offices: Let us show you them From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices Our home offices range from tasteful to “please explain yourself.” Since its beginnings in 1998, Ars has never had a single, central office—a setup that makes for a great commute to work, with little risk of getting stuck in traffic.

As Ars staffers step away from their desks for a few days to spend some time with family and friends, we wanted to give you a look inside our home offices. We’ve got all sorts of setups, tucked into basements, dens, spare bedrooms, apartment corners, and lofts.

sport.title: Alex Eala shares how it feels to be a part of a golden generation of sport in the Philippines, ‘we’re all exce
paras: Alexandra Eala’s season may be officially over, but she is far from enjoying the relaxation she has earned. After all, her schedule is perhaps the most relentless on the WTA Tour, given what a national treasure she has become in such a short space of time in the Philippines.

Having shot from seemingly relative obscurity to instant superstardom during the 2024 Miami Open, since then, this youngster has only continued to build on that stunning foundation. Now, she sits at a career-high ranking, having just enjoyed her best-ever run at two Grand Slam events, beaten countless top ten players, and won her first WTA Tour-level trophy too.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva’s 2026 Season Recap: Teen Prodigy No More
paras: Andreeva had announced herself in 2025 with back-to-back WTA 1000 titles in Dubai and Indian Wells, and the question hanging over her was whether that surge was a breakthrough or a blip. Four singles titles later — Adelaide, Linz, Roland Garros and the WTA Finals — the answer is emphatic.

Andreeva opened the year in style in Adelaide, falling behind 0-3 to Victoria Mboko in the final before reeling off nine straight games to win 6-3, 6-1. The hard-court spring that followed was bumpier: her title defences in Dubai and Indian Wells fizzled, the latter ending in a third-round loss to Katerina Siniakova.

Italy were still able to make it through this tie after wins for Lorenzo Musetti and a deciding doubles win for Matteo Berrettini and Andrea Vavassori, and Cobolli was not actually too downcast about his own performance either.
